# Unsafe deserialization of HTTP request data (Python)

`qualor:python/unsafe-deserialization` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A08:2025 Software or Data Integrity Failures](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A08_2025-Software_or_Data_Integrity_Failures/), [A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A08_2021-Software_and_Data_Integrity_Failures/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data loaded with a deserializer that can build arbitrary objects: `pickle`,
`marshal`, `shelve`, `dill`, `jsonpickle`, and PyYAML's `yaml.load()` without a loader or with an
unsafe one (`Loader`, `UnsafeLoader`, `FullLoader`). Request data is followed in Flask, Django and
FastAPI, including uploaded files.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
The Python documentation warns that unpickling can run arbitrary code: a pickle names the
functions to call while it is loaded. A client who sends one runs code on the server. The same
holds for `marshal`, `shelve`, `dill`, `jsonpickle` and PyYAML's unsafe loaders.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** the request body is unpickled.

```python
import pickle

from flask import Flask, jsonify, request

app = Flask(__name__)


@app.route("/cart", methods=["POST"])
def save_cart():
    cart = pickle.loads(request.get_data())
    return jsonify(items=len(cart))
```

**Compliant:** the body is parsed as JSON, which yields only plain data.

```python
import json

from flask import Flask, jsonify, request

app = Flask(__name__)


@app.route("/cart", methods=["POST"])
def save_cart():
    cart = json.loads(request.get_data())
    return jsonify(items=len(cart))
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Accept a data-only format: `json.loads()`, `yaml.safe_load()` or
  `yaml.load(x, Loader=yaml.SafeLoader)`, and validate the result (with pydantic, say).
- Never unpickle what a client sent. If the server must get its own objects back from a client,
  sign them and check the signature before loading, or keep the objects on the server and hand out
  an id.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Flask
- Django
- FastAPI
- `pickle`
- `marshal`
- `shelve`
- PyYAML
- jsonpickle
- dill

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A custom YAML loader class built on an unsafe one is not followed.
- A file the server opens by a request-chosen name, and a shelf the request names, are reported,
  since the name could point at an uploaded file.
- A signature check (`hmac.compare_digest`) before loading is not recognised, so the load is still
  reported.
- A slice is followed when it slices request data in place (`request.get_data()[4:]`),
  a variable assigned request data, or a view parameter; a slice of a value built from request
  data (`(request.args["q"] + "x")[:50]`) is missed.
- An allow-list is recognised only as a lookup in a module-level dict of literals assigned to an
  upper-case name that is never changed, or as a ternary of constants.
- Request sources are recognised by their shape: a Flask `<int:n>` route parameter and a numeric
  Django URL argument still count as request data, and a function whose first parameter is named
  `request` in a Django module is taken for a view.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/python/deserialization/unsafe-deserialization.py`](../../../rules/python/deserialization/unsafe-deserialization.py) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.
